items.item: Benchmarks / average cost per hire statistics

Benchmark ranges segmented by role and by hiring volume — all three give one flat benchmark/statistics block, none break cost per hire out by role type or by annual hiring volume the way the distinct angle calls for.
A hard-cost vs. soft-cost line-item framework — competitors categorize by internal/external only; none name the hard-cost/soft-cost split explicitly as its own structure.
A calculator tied back to a pillar's broader cost breakdown — hiretruffle's calculator stands alone; none connect the line items to a wider cost-per-hire pillar the way this asset's angle requires.

What is the average cost per hire in the US?

Defines cost per hire as the average spend to recruit a new employee (typically $4,500-$4,800), via the formula Internal Costs + External Costs / Total Hires; names Internal Costs (prorated recruiter/HR salaries, referral awards, hiring-manager interview time) and External Costs (job board fees, agency/search-firm fees, ATS costs, background checks, candidate travel/relocation); notes cost varies by company size, industry, and role seniority (specialized technical/C-suite: $15k-$30k+); flags quarterly tracking for budget optimization and ROI; points to the SHRM Cost-Per-Hire Standard for a consistent tracking process.
